items.title: Differential privacy, databases, and add/remove adjacency

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Let U be a nonempty record universe and let N0={0,1,2,...}. A database is a finite-support function D:U→N0; D(u) counts occurrences. The domain D of databases has its power-set sigma-algebra. D,D′ are neighbors exactly when one is obtained by adding or removing one occurrence of one record. A mechanism into a measurable output space (Y,B) is a probability kernel K. For ε≥0 and 0≤δ≤1, K is (ε,δ)-DP when K(D,A)≤e^εK(D′,A)+δ for every ordered neighboring pair and every A∈B; δ=0 is pure ε-DP.
proof_obligations: State the add/remove convention, variable-size database domain, output event space, and both DP parameters exactly; distinguish this relation from replace-one adjacency.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Laplace noise distribution

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: For b>0, let Exp(1/b) be the probability law on (0,+∞) with density x↦b⁻¹e^(−x/b). For every Borel set A⊆R, define Lap(b)(A)=½ Exp(1/b)(A∩(0,+∞))+½ Exp(1/b)({x>0:−x∈A}). Define Lap(0) to be the point mass at 0. Thus Lap(b) is the equal mixture of a positive exponential noise law and its reflection.
proof_obligations: Verify that both mixture terms are probability measures on the stated Borel output space and that the zero-scale branch is a probability measure.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the published construction of the real exponential probability law; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

items.title: Global L1 sensitivity

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Let d≥1 and let f:D→R^d be a query on the database domain with add/remove adjacency. When the set of adjacent-pair differences has an attained finite maximum, the global L1 sensitivity of f is Δ₁f=max_{D∼D′}||f(D)−f(D′)||₁, where ||x||₁=∑_{j=1}^d|x_j|. The sensitivity is finite when this maximum is finite.
proof_obligations: Specify the finite-dimensional query codomain, adjacency relation, and attainment/finite-value condition needed for the maximum to be defined.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Laplace noise has its stated Lebesgue density

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: For every b>0, the probability measure Lap(b) is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure on R and has density z↦(2b)⁻¹exp(−|z|/b).
proof_obligations: Derive the positive and reflected negative half-line densities from the exponential density and reflection invariance; handle the singleton {0}.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the exponential-law and Lebesgue-reflection suppliers.

items.title: Finite independent Laplace noise has product density

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: For b>0 and finite d≥1, the product probability law Lap(b)^{⊗d} on R^d has Lebesgue density z↦(2b)⁻ᵈexp(−||z||₁/b); its coordinate projections are independent and each has law Lap(b).
proof_obligations: Show the product density integrates to one, agrees with the finite product Laplace law on measurable rectangles, and therefore agrees on the product sigma-algebra.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the real exponential/Lebesgue suppliers; finite product formation adds no stronger choice principle.

items.title: Laplace mechanism

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Input a database D, a finite-dimensional query f:D→R^d with finite global L1 sensitivity Δ₁f, and ε>0. If Δ₁f>0, draw Z from the finite product law Lap(Δ₁f/ε)^{⊗d} and release f(D)+Z. If Δ₁f=0, release f(D) deterministically. The output space is R^d with its Borel sigma-algebra.
proof_obligations: Give the exact noise scale, independent-coordinate law, zero-sensitivity branch, and measurable output space; justify the probability-kernel construction from the finite product law.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the real Laplace probability law; the finite product and mechanism construction use no stronger choice principle.

items.title: Laplace mechanism privacy

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: For every finite-dimensional query f with finite global L1 sensitivity and every ε>0, the Laplace mechanism is (ε,0)-differentially private under add/remove adjacency.
proof_obligations: Prove the positive-sensitivity density-ratio bound in both directions, integrate over every Borel event, and handle Δ₁f=0 separately.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the real-valued Laplace mechanism; the privacy-ratio argument itself is choice-free.

items.title: Exponential-mechanism utility sensitivity

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Let R be a nonempty finite set independent of the database, and let u:D×R→R be a real-valued utility. When the adjacent-pair utility-difference set has an attained finite maximum, its global utility sensitivity is Δᵤ=max_{D∼D′, r∈R}|u(D,r)−u(D′,r)|.
proof_obligations: State database-independent finite range, real-valued utility, add/remove adjacency, and the attained finite maximum convention; the exponential mechanism below requires Δᵤ>0.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Exponential mechanism

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Input D, ε>0, a nonempty finite database-independent range R, and utility u with finite positive global utility sensitivity Δᵤ. For each r∈R set w_D(r)=exp(εu(D,r)/(2Δᵤ)), set Z_D=∑_{s∈R}w_D(s), and output r with probability w_D(r)/Z_D. Since R is finite nonempty and all scores are real, 0<Z_D<∞.
proof_obligations: Verify the finite positive normalization and keep the database-independent range and positive-sensitivity hypotheses explicit.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Exponential mechanism privacy and utility

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Under the exponential-mechanism hypotheses, the output law is (ε,0)-differentially private. For D fixed, let R_OPT={r∈R:u(D,r)=OPTᵤ(D)}. For every t>0, P[u(D,M(D))≤OPTᵤ(D)−(2Δᵤ/ε)(ln(|R|/|R_OPT|)+t)]≤e^(−t).
proof_obligations: Bound both the point-probability and normalizer ratios; for utility, bound bad unnormalized mass and lower-bound the normalizer using all maximizers; verify R_OPT is nonempty.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Differential privacy inequality for bounded measurable functions

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Let P,Q be probability measures and suppose P(A)≤e^εQ(A)+δ for every measurable A, with ε≥0 and 0≤δ≤1. Then for every measurable g with 0≤g≤1, ∫g dP≤e^ε∫g dQ+δ.
proof_obligations: Approximate g from below by dyadic simple functions, apply the event inequality to each level set, and pass to the limit by monotone convergence.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Differential privacy is preserved under randomized postprocessing

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: If K is an (ε,δ)-differentially private probability kernel from databases to a measurable output space and L is any data-independent probability kernel from that output space to another measurable space, then the composed kernel KL is (ε,δ)-differentially private.
proof_obligations: For each output event B, apply the bounded-function extension to g(y)=L(y,B), then identify the integrals with the composed-kernel event probabilities.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Pure differential privacy bounds relative entropy

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy

items.statement_or_definition: Let P and Q be probability measures on a standard-Borel space satisfying P(A)≤e^εQ(A) and Q(A)≤e^εP(A) for every measurable A, where ε≥0. Then D(P||Q)≤ε(e^ε−1).
proof_obligations: Construct common Radon–Nikodym densities, derive the pointwise likelihood-ratio bounds, bound the symmetrized KL integrand, and establish nonnegativity of the reverse KL.
items.axiom_use: AC is used for the Radon–Nikodym densities; no stronger axiom is used.

items.title: Approximate-DP kernels admit a nearby pure-DP kernel on standard-Borel targets

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy

items.statement_or_definition: Let H and Y be standard-Borel spaces, λ a probability measure on H, and K,L probability kernels H→Y. If for λ-almost every h the pair K(h,·),L(h,·) satisfies both (ε,δ)-DP event inequalities, then there is a probability kernel K* such that for λ-almost every h and every measurable A, e^(−ε)L(h,A)≤K*(h,A)≤e^εL(h,A), and ∫TV(K(h,·),K*(h,·))λ(dh)≤δ, where TV(P,Q)=sup_A|P(A)−Q(A)|.
proof_obligations: Use jointly measurable Radon–Nikodym densities relative to (K+L)/2, clip the density into [e^(−ε)q,e^εq], renormalize within the available slack, prove TV≤δ, and define the kernel measurably on one common conull set.
items.axiom_use: AC is used through the published jointly measurable RN-kernel supplier and the countable measure-determining algebra; no additional choice principle is used.

items.title: Basic adaptive composition

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Let k≥1 mechanisms be adaptively composed, with round i conditional on every prior transcript being (εᵢ,δᵢ)-differentially private under the same neighboring-database relation. If εᵢ≥0, δᵢ≥0, and ∑ᵢδᵢ≤1, then the full transcript is (∑ᵢεᵢ,∑ᵢδᵢ)-differentially private.
proof_obligations: Prove by induction on k; cap each conditional future-event probability at one, apply the bounded-function extension to the prefix kernel, and identify the iterated-kernel event probability.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Advanced adaptive composition for standard-Borel outputs

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Assume AC. Let each round output space and every finite transcript-prefix space be standard Borel. For k≥1 adaptive rounds, if each round conditional on every prior transcript is (ε,δ)-differentially private, where ε≥0, 0≤δ≤1, and 0<δ′<1 with kδ+δ′≤1, then the full transcript is (ε′,kδ+δ′)-differentially private, where ε′=√(2k ln(1/δ′))ε+kε(e^ε−1).
proof_obligations: For the pure case, factor the transcript likelihood ratio into conditional RN ratios, bound their conditional KL means and apply Azuma. For approximate DP, purify each round under a base law dominating original and modified transcript prefixes, bound prefix TV cumulatively by kδ, then compose the pure result.
items.axiom_use: Assume full AC for the measurable RN-kernel versions and Azuma supplier. The standard-Borel output assumption is explicit and is the current scope boundary.

items.title: Approximate privacy admits purification of a joint measure with fixed history marginal
items.axiom_use: AC is used only through the ordinary finite-measure Radon–Nikodym theorem. No regular conditional distribution or kernel Radon–Nikodym version is used.

references.title: Dwork and Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy, Lemma 3.17 and Theorem 3.20

items.statement_or_definition:
Assume AC. Let $H,Y$ be arbitrary measurable spaces, let $\lambda$ be a probability measure on $H$, and let $K,L$ be probability kernels from $H$ to $Y$. Suppose $\varepsilon\ge0$, $0\le\delta\le1$, and, for every $h$ and every measurable $A\subseteq Y$,
$$K(h,A)\le e^\varepsilon L(h,A)+\delta,\qquad L(h,A)\le e^\varepsilon K(h,A)+\delta.$$
Define probability measures on the product sigma-algebra by
$$R(B)=\int_H K(h,B_h)\lambda(dh),\qquad S(B)=\int_H L(h,B_h)\lambda(dh).$$
There is a probability measure $T$ on $H\times Y$ whose $H$ marginal is $\lambda$, such that, as inequalities of measures,
$$e^{-\varepsilon}S\le T\le e^\varepsilon S,\qquad \operatorname{TV}(R,T)\le\delta.$$
Here $\operatorname{TV}(U,V)=\sup_B|U(B)-V(B)|$. No countability or topological condition is imposed on either measurable space.
proof_obligations: Construct ordinary joint-measure RN densities, and bound conditional clipping excesses by localized section-event inequalities.
Give measurable mass correction within [q/a,aq], including a=1, preserve the history marginal, and prove TV≤δ without disintegration.

items.title: Advanced adaptive composition on arbitrary measurable output spaces
items.axiom_use: AC is used through ordinary finite-measure Radon–Nikodym derivatives and the Azuma supplier. No kernel Radon–Nikodym version or regular conditional law is used.

references.title: Dwork and Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy, Theorem 3.20
Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, Lemma 2.4 and Claim 2.5

items.statement_or_definition:
Assume AC. Let $\mathcal D$ be a set equipped with its power-set sigma-algebra and a symmetric adjacency relation $\sim$; this includes finite-support record-count databases with neighbors differing by one added or removed occurrence. Let $k\ge1$, let $Y_1,\ldots,Y_k$ be arbitrary measurable output spaces, and let round $i$ be a probability kernel $K_i(D,h,\cdot)$ on $Y_i$, measurable in the previous transcript $h\in H_{i-1}=\prod_{j<i}Y_j$ for each database $D$. Suppose that for every ordered neighboring pair $D\sim D'$, every $i$, every $h$, and every measurable $A\subseteq Y_i$,
$$K_i(D,h,A)\le e^\varepsilon K_i(D',h,A)+\delta,$$
where $\varepsilon\ge0$ and $0\le\delta\le1$. If $0<\delta'<1$ and $k\delta+\delta'\le1$, then the full transcript, on the finite product sigma-algebra, is $(\varepsilon',k\delta+\delta')$-differentially private, where
$$\varepsilon'=\varepsilon\sqrt{2k\ln(1/\delta')}+k\varepsilon(e^\varepsilon-1).$$
proof_obligations: Construct the finite original and modified prefix laws on arbitrary measurable product spaces.
Prove the global RN density chain relative to the original reference path law and TV contraction recursion with total error kδ.
Prove conditional normalization, entropy drift≤ε(e^ε−1), and actual conditional-expectation integral identities.
Apply Azuma with increment interval width2ε, handle ε=0, repeat with databases swapped, and derive the exact advanced parameters.

items.title: Basic and advanced adaptive composition

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition:
Let databases be finite-support record-count functions, with neighbors differing by one added or removed record occurrence. For $k\ge1$, let round $i$ be a probability kernel $K_i(D,h,\cdot)$ from the $i$th arbitrary measurable output space, conditional on every prior transcript $h$. Suppose that for every ordered neighboring pair $D\sim D'$, every $h$, and every measurable round-$i$ event $A$,
$$
K_i(D,h,A)\le e^{\varepsilon_i}K_i(D',h,A)+\delta_i,
$$
where $\varepsilon_i\ge0$ and $\delta_i\ge0$. If $\sum_i\delta_i\le1$, the full transcript on the finite product sigma-algebra is $(\sum_i\varepsilon_i,\sum_i\delta_i)$-differentially private. Also, assuming AC, if every conditional round has the same parameters $(\varepsilon,\delta)$ with $\varepsilon\ge0$ and $0\le\delta\le1$, then for any $0<\delta'<1$ with $k\delta+\delta'\le1$, advanced composition on arbitrary measurable output spaces gives parameters $(\varepsilon',k\delta+\delta')$, where
$$
\varepsilon'=\sqrt{2k\ln(1/\delta')}\,\varepsilon+k\varepsilon(e^\varepsilon-1).
$$
proof_obligations: Apply the proved arbitrary-output basic and advanced suppliers with their complete hypotheses, declaring AC only for the advanced clause.
items.axiom_use: The basic clause is choice-free. Assume AC for the advanced clause, through the ordinary finite-measure Radon–Nikodym theorem and Azuma supplier; no regular conditional law is used.

items.title: Record-level scope and limits of differential privacy

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: The definition on this page is central, record-level privacy for add/remove adjacency. It does not by itself define client-level or local privacy, and keeping data on a device or applying secure aggregation does not establish the event inequalities in this definition. Differential privacy limits the effect of one record on a release; it does not prevent conclusions about an attribute that is strongly correlated with other records or public information.
proof_obligations: Keep central record adjacency distinct from local randomization and secure aggregation; preserve the correlated-attribute limitation without claiming unconditional secrecy.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

title: Differential privacy mechanisms and composition — Examples

items.title: Add/remove noisy count

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: For a predicate P on U that is satisfied by at least one possible record, let f(D) count the records of D satisfying P. Its add/remove global L1 sensitivity is 1, so for ε>0 the scalar Laplace mechanism releases f(D)+Z with Z∼Lap(1/ε) and is (ε,0)-differentially private.
proof_obligations: Verify the count changes by at most one and that a satisfying record witnesses attainment of sensitivity one; instantiate the proved Laplace theorem at that sensitivity.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Laplace noise law; the sensitivity calculation is choice-free.

items.title: Finite-range private selection

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Let R={a,b} and ε>0. The constant utility u(D,a)=1,u(D,b)=0 has Δᵤ=0 and is inadmissible for the positive-sensitivity exponential mechanism. Fix a record u* and set s(D)=1 exactly when D(u*)>0; define instead u(D,a)=1,u(D,b)=1−s(D). Then Δᵤ=1, the mechanism is (ε,0)-differentially private, and it selects a with probability e^(ε/2)/(e^(ε/2)+e^(ε(1−s(D))/2)).
proof_obligations: Check the first assignment has zero sensitivity and is excluded; for the second, compute Δᵤ=1, normalize both weights, and instantiate the privacy theorem.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.

items.title: Thresholding a private noisy count

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Release a Laplace-noised count of records satisfying a fixed predicate, then output 1 exactly when the released real number is at least a fixed threshold c∈R. The threshold decision is a data-independent deterministic postprocessing of the private noisy count and retains the same (ε,0) guarantee.
proof_obligations: Identify the threshold map as a Borel-measurable deterministic kernel independent of the database, then apply the Laplace and postprocessing theorems.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Laplace noise law.

items.title: Record-level versus client-level adjacency

references.title: Cynthia Dwork and Aaron Roth, The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy
Salil Vadhan, The Complexity of Differential Privacy, 2017 manuscript

items.statement_or_definition: Suppose a client contributes 100 records to a database. Under the page definition, adding or removing one of those records is one neighboring step; adding or removing the client’s full 100-record contribution is not one neighboring step. A client-level guarantee therefore requires a client-level adjacency relation and a proof using that relation.
proof_obligations: Count the changed records in each comparison and identify which one satisfies the stated adjacency definition; make no client-level privacy claim from record-level DP.
items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used.
